documents.title: The Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan
documents.summary: The supreme law of Pakistan: fundamental rights, principles of policy, federal and provincial structure, Islamic provisions and the amendments that reshaped it. Cite articles by number in Pakistan Affairs, Constitutional Law and governance answers.

documents.title: The Objectives Resolution
documents.summary: Moved by Liaquat Ali Khan and adopted on 12 March 1949, it declared sovereignty belongs to Allah and set the Islamic and democratic principles for future constitutions; it was preamble to the 1956, 1962 and 1973 constitutions and became a substantive part via Article 2A in 1985.
documents.source: pakistani.org (annex to the Constitution of Pakistan)

documents.title: Lahore Resolution (Pakistan Resolution) of the All-India Muslim League
documents.summary: Adopted at the League's Lahore session (22 to 24 March 1940), it demanded that Muslim-majority areas in the north-west and east be grouped into 'independent states'; 23 March is marked as Pakistan Day and the text's wording is a frequent exam question.
documents.source: indiaofthepast.org (transcription; no official Pakistani host found)

documents.title: The Constitution (Eighteenth Amendment) Act, 2010 (Act No. X of 2010)
documents.summary: Restored the parliamentary character of the 1973 Constitution, removed the President's power to dissolve the National Assembly (Art. 58(2)(b)), abolished the Concurrent List and devolved major subjects to the provinces; central to any question on federalism and provincial autonomy.
documents.source: National Assembly of Pakistan (Gazette of Pakistan)

documents.title: Charter of the United Nations and Statute of the International Court of Justice
documents.summary: The founding treaty of the UN: sovereign equality, the ban on the use of force (Art. 2(4)), self-defence (Art. 51) and the powers of the Security Council. The backbone of answers in International Relations and International Law.

documents.title: Universal Declaration of Human Rights
documents.summary: The first global statement of the rights every person holds, the basis of later human rights treaties. Useful for essays and for Gender Studies, International Law and Constitutional Law comparisons.

documents.title: The Indus Waters Treaty 1960 (between India, Pakistan and the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development)
documents.issuer: Government of India, Government of Pakistan and the World Bank (IBRD), Karachi
documents.summary: Allocates the Eastern Rivers (Ravi, Beas, Sutlej) to India and the Western Rivers (Indus, Jhelum, Chenab) to Pakistan with dispute-settlement machinery; India's 2025 move to hold it 'in abeyance' makes it a top current-affairs topic. Linked text is the treaty as registered in the UN Treaty Series.

documents.title: National Security Policy of Pakistan 2022-2026 (public version)
documents.issuer: National Security Division, Government of Pakistan
documents.summary: Pakistan's first National Security Policy, placing economic security at the core of a comprehensive (citizen-centric) security concept; widely examined in current affairs and international relations.
documents.source: Office of the National Security Adviser (onsa.gov.pk, archived copy; original domain offline)

documents.title: Pakistan Economic Survey 2025-26
documents.summary: The government's annual review of the economy released before the budget (June 2026), with chapters on growth, agriculture, fiscal policy, debt, inflation, trade, education, health, energy and climate; the standard source for current economic figures.

documents.title: Paris Agreement
documents.issuer: Conference of the Parties to the UNFCCC (COP 21)
documents.summary: Commits all parties to hold warming well below 2°C and pursue 1.5°C through nationally determined contributions, with a global stocktake and Article 6 carbon markets; central to climate questions after Pakistan's 2022 floods.

documents.title: Transforming our world: the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development (A/RES/70/1)
documents.summary: Sets out the 17 Sustainable Development Goals and 169 targets for 2030; Pakistan adopted the SDGs through a National Assembly resolution in 2016, and they recur across essay, economics and governance papers.

documents.title: Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons
documents.issuer: Opened for signature in London, Moscow and Washington (UN General Assembly commended it in resolution 2373 (XXII))
documents.summary: Rests on three pillars: non-proliferation, disarmament (Art. VI) and peaceful use of nuclear energy; Pakistan, India and Israel never joined, central to South Asian nuclear debates.

documents.title: The Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, 1956
documents.summary: Pakistan's first constitution, in force from 23 March 1956 (Republic Day) until abrogated in October 1958; it introduced the parliamentary system, the 'Islamic Republic' name and parity between East and West Pakistan.

documents.title: The Constitution of the Republic of Pakistan, 1962
documents.issuer: Government of Pakistan (promulgated by President Ayub Khan)
documents.summary: Ayub Khan's presidential constitution, in force from 8 June 1962 until abrogated in March 1969; it rested on indirect elections through Basic Democracies and a strong executive, a frequent comparison point with 1956 and 1973.

documents.title: The Constitution (Twenty-sixth Amendment) Act, 2024 (Act No. XXVI of 2024)
documents.summary: Created constitutional benches, changed the appointment of the Chief Justice of Pakistan through a Special Parliamentary Committee, restructured the Judicial Commission and added Article 9A (right to a clean and healthy environment); a major current-affairs topic on judicial independence.
documents.source: National Assembly of Pakistan (Gazette of Pakistan)

documents.title: Presidential Address of Allama Muhammad Iqbal to the All-India Muslim League, Allahabad (29 December 1930)
documents.summary: Iqbal's address proposing a consolidated North-West Indian Muslim state, widely cited as the intellectual basis of the Pakistan idea; the linked Iqbal Academy Pakistan volume compiles the address with related League documents.

documents.title: Address of Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah to the First Constituent Assembly of Pakistan, 11 August 1947
documents.summary: Jinnah's first address as President of the Constituent Assembly, setting out equal citizenship regardless of religion, rule of law and the fight against corruption and nepotism; central to debates on the state's ideology and minority rights.

documents.title: Pakistan Penal Code, 1860
documents.summary: The main substantive criminal law defining offences and punishments, including the Hudood-era and blasphemy provisions added later; the core text for criminology and criminal law papers.
documents.source: Pakistan Code (Ministry of Law and Justice)

documents.title: Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898
documents.issuer: Governor-General of India in Council (adapted by Pakistan)
documents.summary: Procedural law for investigation, arrest, bail, trial and appeal in criminal cases; essential for understanding policing, FIRs and the criminal justice system.
documents.source: Pakistan Code (Ministry of Law and Justice)

documents.title: Qanun-e-Shahadat Order, 1984
documents.summary: Pakistan's law of evidence, which replaced the Evidence Act 1872 and brought rules on witnesses and proof in line with Islamic injunctions; tested in law and criminology papers.
documents.source: Pakistan Code (Ministry of Law and Justice)

documents.title: Contract Act, 1872
documents.issuer: Governor-General of India in Council (adapted by Pakistan)
documents.summary: Defines offer, acceptance, consideration, capacity, void and voidable agreements, breach and remedies, plus indemnity, guarantee, bailment and agency; the foundation of mercantile law.
documents.source: Pakistan Code (Ministry of Law and Justice)

documents.title: Sale of Goods Act, 1930
documents.summary: Governs contracts for the sale of goods: conditions and warranties, transfer of ownership, and rights of an unpaid seller; a standard mercantile law topic.
documents.source: Pakistan Code (Ministry of Law and Justice)

documents.title: Partnership Act, 1932
documents.summary: Regulates formation of partnerships, rights and liabilities of partners, registration of firms and dissolution; a standard mercantile law and business topic.
documents.source: Pakistan Code (Ministry of Law and Justice)

documents.title: Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881
documents.issuer: Governor-General of India in Council (adapted by Pakistan)
documents.summary: Governs promissory notes, bills of exchange and cheques, including endorsement, holder in due course and dishonour; a core mercantile law and banking topic.
documents.source: Pakistan Code (Ministry of Law and Justice)

documents.title: Companies Act, 2017
documents.summary: Replaced the Companies Ordinance 1984 as the law on incorporation, governance, audit and winding up of companies, administered by the SECP; key for corporate law and auditing.
documents.source: Pakistan Code (Ministry of Law and Justice)

documents.title: Muslim Family Laws Ordinance, 1961
documents.issuer: President of Pakistan (Field Marshal Ayub Khan)
documents.summary: Regulates marriage registration, polygamy (Arbitration Council permission), talaq procedure, maintenance and inheritance of orphaned grandchildren; central to Muslim law and gender studies.
documents.source: Pakistan Code (Ministry of Law and Justice)

documents.title: Dissolution of Muslim Marriages Act, 1939
documents.summary: Lists the grounds on which a Muslim wife may obtain dissolution of marriage through the courts; a staple of Muslim law and gender studies.
documents.source: Pakistan Code (Ministry of Law and Justice)

documents.title: Anti-Terrorism Act, 1997
documents.summary: Defines terrorism, sets up anti-terrorism courts and provides for proscribing organisations (First Schedule) and the Fourth Schedule watch list; key for internal security questions.
documents.source: Pakistan Code (Ministry of Law and Justice)

documents.title: National Counter Terrorism Authority (NACTA) Act, 2013
documents.summary: Established NACTA to coordinate counter-terrorism and counter-extremism strategy and to monitor the National Action Plan; useful with questions on internal security architecture.
documents.source: Pakistan Code (Ministry of Law and Justice)

documents.title: Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act, 2016
documents.summary: Pakistan's cybercrime law covering unauthorised access, cyber-terrorism, online harassment and fake information, with FIA powers; debated over free-speech concerns and later amendments.
documents.source: Pakistan Code (Ministry of Law and Justice)

documents.title: Right of Access to Information Act, 2017
documents.short: Right of Access to Information Act 2017
documents.summary: Gives citizens the right to obtain information held by federal public bodies and created the Pakistan Information Commission, giving effect to Article 19A; a governance and transparency topic.
documents.source: Pakistan Code (Ministry of Law and Justice)

documents.title: Protection against Harassment of Women at the Workplace Act, 2010
documents.summary: Requires organisations to adopt a code of conduct and inquiry committees and created the Federal Ombudsperson for workplace harassment; a key gender studies law.
documents.source: Pakistan Code (Ministry of Law and Justice)

documents.title: Police Order, 2002
documents.issuer: Chief Executive of Pakistan (General Pervez Musharraf)
documents.summary: Replaced the Police Act 1861 with a framework of public safety commissions, police complaints authorities and separation of investigation from watch-and-ward; core to police reform questions.
documents.source: Pakistan Code (Ministry of Law and Justice)

documents.title: Elections Act, 2017
documents.summary: Consolidated eight earlier election laws covering the Election Commission, delimitation, electoral rolls, conduct of polls, political parties and election offences.
documents.source: Pakistan Code (Ministry of Law and Justice)

documents.title: Civil Servants Act, 1973
documents.summary: Governs the terms and conditions of federal civil servants (appointment, probation, promotion, retirement and conduct); directly relevant to CSS aspirants and public administration.
documents.source: Pakistan Code (Ministry of Law and Justice)

documents.title: Pakistan Electronic Media Regulatory Authority Ordinance, 2002
documents.summary: Created PEMRA to license and regulate private TV, radio and distribution services; the basis for questions on media freedom and broadcast regulation.
documents.source: Pakistan Code (Ministry of Law and Justice)

documents.title: Pakistan Environmental Protection Act, 1997
documents.summary: Framework environmental law establishing the Pakistan Environmental Protection Agency and Council, National Environmental Quality Standards and EIA requirements.
documents.source: Pakistan Code (Ministry of Law and Justice)

documents.title: National Accountability Ordinance, 1999
documents.summary: Created the National Accountability Bureau and the offence of corruption and corrupt practices, with accountability courts; repeatedly amended and central to anti-corruption debates.
documents.source: Pakistan Code (Ministry of Law and Justice)

documents.title: National Action Plan, 2014 (20-point counter-terrorism plan)
documents.summary: Twenty-point counter-terrorism plan agreed after the December 2014 Army Public School attack, covering military courts, terror financing, madrassa regulation and hate speech; the NACTA page lists all 20 points.

documents.title: National Climate Change Policy (Updated October 2021)
documents.issuer: Ministry of Climate Change, Government of Pakistan
documents.summary: Updated version of the 2012 policy setting adaptation and mitigation measures across water, agriculture, energy, forestry and disaster management; the main reference for climate questions on Pakistan.
documents.source: Ministry of Climate Change and Environmental Coordination

documents.title: National Adaptation Plan Pakistan 2023
documents.issuer: Ministry of Climate Change and Environmental Coordination, Government of Pakistan
documents.summary: Pakistan's first National Adaptation Plan, approved by the federal cabinet in July 2023 after the 2022 floods, setting adaptation priorities in agriculture, water, urban resilience, health and disaster risk management.
documents.source: Ministry of Climate Change and Environmental Coordination

documents.title: Pakistan Updated Nationally Determined Contributions 2021
documents.issuer: Ministry of Climate Change, Government of Pakistan
documents.summary: Pakistan's Paris Agreement pledge, with a conditional target to cut projected 2030 emissions by 50% and shift to renewables and electric vehicles; useful for climate diplomacy questions.
documents.source: Ministry of Climate Change and Environmental Coordination

documents.title: National Forest Policy 2015
documents.issuer: Ministry of Climate Change, Government of Pakistan
documents.summary: Sets a national framework for expanding and protecting forest cover, watershed management and REDD+, noting forestry is a provincial subject after the 18th Amendment.
documents.source: Ministry of Climate Change and Environmental Coordination

documents.title: National Food Security Policy
documents.issuer: Ministry of National Food Security and Research, Government of Pakistan
documents.summary: Pakistan's first national food security policy, built on availability, access, utilisation and stability of food, with targets for agricultural growth and a proposed National Food Security Council.
documents.source: Ministry of National Food Security and Research (mnfsr.gov.pk, archived copy)

documents.title: National Education Policy 2009
documents.issuer: Ministry of Education, Government of Pakistan
documents.summary: The last full National Education Policy approved by the federal government, setting targets for enrolment, literacy, curriculum and spending (7% of GDP goal); the 2017 policy and a 2026 policy were released only as drafts.
documents.source: Ministry of Federal Education and Professional Training

documents.title: Pakistan National Education Policy Framework 2018
documents.issuer: Ministry of Federal Education and Professional Training, Government of Pakistan
documents.summary: Framework setting four priorities: reducing out-of-school children, uniform education standards, improving quality, and skills/higher education; context for the Single National Curriculum.
documents.source: Ministry of Federal Education and Professional Training

documents.title: National Health Vision Pakistan 2016-2025
documents.issuer: Ministry of National Health Services, Regulations and Coordination, Government of Pakistan
documents.summary: Federal-provincial vision launched in 2016 to guide health policy after devolution, aimed at universal health coverage and the SDG health targets.

documents.title: National Gender Policy Framework
documents.issuer: Ministry of Planning, Development and Special Initiatives (Planning Commission)
documents.summary: Launched on 8 March 2022, it sets gender-equality policy actions in education, health, economic empowerment, political participation, safety and governance.

documents.title: National Electricity Policy 2021
documents.issuer: Power Division, Ministry of Energy, Government of Pakistan (approved by the Council of Common Interests)
documents.summary: Current national power-sector policy approved by the CCI in 2021, covering generation planning, competitive markets, circular debt, affordability and renewable integration.

documents.title: National Artificial Intelligence Policy 2025
documents.issuer: Ministry of IT and Telecommunication, Government of Pakistan
documents.summary: Approved by the federal cabinet in July 2025, it sets goals for AI skills, research, an AI innovation fund and responsible AI governance.

documents.title: Digital Pakistan Policy
documents.issuer: Ministry of IT and Telecommunication, Government of Pakistan
documents.summary: Policy for a digital economy covering e-government, broadband, IT exports, digital skills and e-commerce; background for questions on digital governance.

documents.title: Uraan Pakistan: 5Es National Economic Transformation Plan 2024-2029
documents.issuer: Ministry of Planning, Development and Special Initiatives
documents.summary: Launched on 31 December 2024, the government's economic plan built on the 5Es (Exports, E-Pakistan, Environment, Energy and Infrastructure, Equity and Empowerment).

documents.title: 13th Five-Year Plan (2024-2029)
documents.issuer: Planning Commission, Ministry of Planning, Development and Special Initiatives
documents.summary: The medium-term development plan that puts Uraan Pakistan into effect, with sector-wise targets and public investment priorities (large PDF).

documents.title: Pakistan Vision 2025: One Nation, One Vision
documents.issuer: Ministry of Planning, Development and Reform, Government of Pakistan
documents.summary: Long-term development vision launched in 2014, built on seven pillars including people first, growth, governance, energy, water and food security, and regional connectivity.

documents.title: Long Term Plan for China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (2017-2030)
documents.issuer: Ministry of Planning, Development and Reform (Pakistan) and National Development and Reform Commission (China)
documents.summary: Joint plan setting CPEC's spatial layout, priority sectors (connectivity, energy, industrial zones, agriculture, tourism) and phases to 2030; core for questions on CPEC and Pakistan-China relations.

documents.title: Federal Budget 2026-27: Budget in Brief
documents.summary: Summary of the federal budget for FY2026-27: revenues, expenditure, fiscal deficit target and financing plan; the quickest official source for budget numbers.

documents.title: Report of the National Finance Commission 2009 (7th NFC Award)
documents.issuer: National Finance Commission, Government of Pakistan
documents.summary: The award agreed in December 2009 that raised the provinces' share of the divisible pool and introduced multiple criteria (population, poverty, revenue, inverse population density); central to fiscal federalism questions.

documents.title: State Bank of Pakistan Annual Report 2025-26: The State of Pakistan's Economy
documents.summary: The central bank's statutory annual assessment of growth, inflation, monetary policy, the fiscal position and external sector for FY26.

documents.title: 7th Population and Housing Census 2023 (First-ever Digital Census): National Census Report
documents.summary: National report of Pakistan's first digital census, with population size, growth rate, urbanisation, literacy, housing and demographic data.

documents.title: Pakistan National Human Development Report 2020: The Three Ps of Inequality: Power, People, and Policy (Overview)
documents.summary: UNDP's report on inequality in Pakistan, estimating elite privilege at about 8% of GDP and comparing human development across quintiles and provinces.

documents.title: Pakistan Floods 2022: Post-Disaster Needs Assessment (PDNA), Supplemental Report
documents.issuer: Government of Pakistan with ADB, EU, UNDP and World Bank
documents.summary: Sector-by-sector supplement to the joint government and donor assessment of damages, losses and recovery needs from the 2022 floods (the main PDNA put damages at about US$14.9 billion and losses at about US$15.2 billion); key evidence for climate vulnerability questions.

documents.title: Statute of the International Court of Justice
documents.issuer: United Nations Conference on International Organization (annexed to the UN Charter)
documents.summary: Founding text of the UN's principal judicial organ; Article 38(1) lists the sources of international law (treaties, custom, general principles, judicial decisions and teachings), a staple exam question.

documents.title: Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties
documents.issuer: United Nations Conference on the Law of Treaties
documents.summary: The 'treaty on treaties': codifies how treaties are made, interpreted, reserved against, amended and terminated, including pacta sunt servanda and jus cogens; essential for any treaty-law question (e.g. Indus Waters Treaty suspension debates).

documents.title: Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations
documents.issuer: United Nations Conference on Diplomatic Intercourse and Immunities
documents.summary: Codifies the law of diplomatic missions: inviolability of premises, diplomatic immunity, persona non grata and the functions of embassies; frequently tested in international law and diplomacy questions.

documents.title: United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea
documents.issuer: Third United Nations Conference on the Law of the Sea
documents.summary: The 'constitution for the oceans': defines territorial sea, contiguous zone, EEZ, continental shelf and high seas, and set up ITLOS; relevant to Pakistan's continental shelf extension and South China Sea disputes.
documents.source: United Nations (Division for Ocean Affairs and the Law of the Sea)

documents.title: Rome Statute of the International Criminal Court
documents.issuer: United Nations Diplomatic Conference of Plenipotentiaries on the Establishment of an International Criminal Court
documents.summary: Created the permanent International Criminal Court with jurisdiction over genocide, crimes against humanity, war crimes and aggression; key to questions on international criminal justice and accountability.

documents.title: Convention on Rights and Duties of States (Montevideo Convention)
documents.issuer: Seventh International Conference of American States
documents.summary: Its Article 1 gives the classic criteria of statehood (permanent population, defined territory, government, capacity to enter into relations with other states), the standard reference in recognition and statehood questions.

documents.title: Geneva Conventions of 12 August 1949 (I–IV)
documents.issuer: Diplomatic Conference of Geneva (depositary: Switzerland; ICRC)
documents.summary: The four conventions protecting wounded and sick soldiers, shipwrecked, prisoners of war and civilians form the core of international humanitarian law; Common Article 3 applies to non-international armed conflicts.
documents.source: International Committee of the Red Cross

documents.title: Protocols Additional to the Geneva Conventions of 12 August 1949 (Protocols I and II)
documents.issuer: Diplomatic Conference on the Reaffirmation and Development of IHL (depositary: Switzerland)
documents.summary: Protocol I strengthens protection in international armed conflicts (distinction, proportionality); Protocol II covers non-international armed conflicts; Pakistan has signed but not ratified them, a useful exam detail.

documents.title: Convention (IV) respecting the Laws and Customs of War on Land and its annex: Regulations (Hague Convention IV)
documents.issuer: Second International Peace Conference, The Hague
documents.summary: The Hague Regulations on the conduct of hostilities and military occupation, now regarded as customary international law; the root of 'Hague law' alongside the Geneva Conventions.

documents.title: 2005 World Summit Outcome (A/RES/60/1), incl. paras 138–139 on the Responsibility to Protect
documents.summary: Paragraphs 138–139 are the agreed UN basis of the Responsibility to Protect populations from genocide, war crimes, ethnic cleansing and crimes against humanity; central to debates on sovereignty and humanitarian intervention.

documents.title: International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights
documents.summary: Binding treaty on civil and political rights (life, fair trial, expression, religion, self-determination in Art. 1); Pakistan ratified in 2010 and reports to the Human Rights Committee.

documents.title: International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights
documents.summary: Binding treaty on rights to work, social security, health, education and an adequate standard of living; Pakistan ratified in 2008, relevant to Article 25A and social-sector questions.

documents.title: Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women
documents.summary: The 'international bill of rights for women', defining discrimination against women and obliging states to end it; Pakistan acceded in 1996 with a declaration subject to its Constitution, a core Gender Studies text.

documents.title: Convention on the Rights of the Child
documents.summary: The most widely ratified human rights treaty, built on the best interests of the child, non-discrimination, survival and participation; Pakistan ratified in 1990 and it informs child-labour and child-marriage laws.

documents.title: Convention against Torture and Other Cruel, Inhuman or Degrading Treatment or Punishment
documents.summary: Defines torture, makes its prohibition absolute and bars returning people to states where they risk torture; Pakistan ratified in 2010 and later enacted the Torture and Custodial Death (Prevention and Punishment) Act 2022.

documents.title: Convention relating to the Status of Refugees
documents.issuer: United Nations Conference of Plenipotentiaries on the Status of Refugees and Stateless Persons
documents.summary: Defines who is a refugee and sets the principle of non-refoulement; Pakistan is not a party despite hosting millions of Afghan refugees, a recurring current-affairs angle.

documents.title: Protocol relating to the Status of Refugees
documents.issuer: United Nations (adopted following UN General Assembly resolution 2198 (XXI))
documents.summary: Removed the 1951 Convention's time limit (events before 1951) and optional geographic limit (Europe), making refugee protection universal.

documents.title: Convention on the Prevention and Punishment of the Crime of Genocide
documents.summary: The first UN human rights treaty, defining genocide and obliging states to prevent and punish it; the basis of cases such as The Gambia v. Myanmar and South Africa v. Israel at the ICJ.

documents.title: International Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Racial Discrimination
documents.summary: Commits states to eliminate racial discrimination in all its forms and set up the CERD Committee; Pakistan ratified it in 1966.

documents.title: Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities
documents.summary: Shifts disability from a charity/medical model to a human rights model, covering accessibility, inclusive education and employment; Pakistan ratified in 2011.

documents.title: Vienna Declaration and Programme of Action
documents.summary: Affirmed that all human rights are universal, indivisible and interdependent, and led to the creation of the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights; often cited in universalism-versus-relativism essays.

documents.title: Comprehensive Nuclear-Test-Ban Treaty
documents.summary: Bans all nuclear explosions; adopted in 1996 but not in force because Annex 2 states including Pakistan, India and the US have not ratified it; relevant to the 1998 tests and test moratoria.

documents.title: Convention on the Prohibition of the Development, Production, Stockpiling and Use of Chemical Weapons and on their Destruction
documents.issuer: Conference on Disarmament / opened for signature in Paris
documents.summary: Bans an entire category of weapons of mass destruction with verification by the OPCW; Pakistan is a state party.
documents.source: Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons

documents.title: Convention on the Prohibition of the Development, Production and Stockpiling of Bacteriological (Biological) and Toxin Weapons and on their Destruction
documents.issuer: Opened for signature in London, Moscow and Washington
documents.summary: The first treaty to ban a whole class of WMD; lacks a verification regime, which is a common critique; Pakistan is a state party.

documents.title: Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons
documents.issuer: United Nations conference to negotiate a legally binding instrument to prohibit nuclear weapons
documents.summary: First treaty to comprehensively ban nuclear weapons, in force since January 2021; no nuclear-armed state, including Pakistan, has joined it.

documents.title: Treaty on Principles Governing the Activities of States in the Exploration and Use of Outer Space, including the Moon and Other Celestial Bodies
documents.summary: Declares outer space the province of all mankind, bans national appropriation and nuclear weapons in orbit; the base of space law, relevant to SUPARCO and space-militarisation debates.
documents.source: UN Office for Outer Space Affairs

documents.title: Security Council Resolution 1373 (2001) on threats to international peace and security caused by terrorist acts
documents.summary: Chapter VII resolution adopted after 9/11 obliging all states to criminalise terrorist financing and deny safe haven; created the Counter-Terrorism Committee and underpins FATF-type obligations.

documents.title: Security Council Resolution 1540 (2004) on non-proliferation of weapons of mass destruction
documents.summary: Requires all states to prevent non-state actors from acquiring nuclear, chemical or biological weapons and to enforce export controls; Pakistan reports to the 1540 Committee.

documents.title: Security Council Resolution 47 (1948) on the India–Pakistan question
documents.summary: Adopted on 21 April 1948, it enlarged UNCIP and set out steps for a ceasefire, withdrawal of forces and a free and impartial plebiscite to decide the accession of Jammu and Kashmir; the foundation of Pakistan's legal position on Kashmir.

documents.title: Resolution of the United Nations Commission for India and Pakistan of 13 August 1948 (in UNCIP report S/1100)
documents.issuer: United Nations Commission for India and Pakistan
documents.summary: Accepted by both governments, it provided for a ceasefire (Part I), a truce agreement (Part II) and reaffirmed that Kashmir's future status be decided by the will of the people (Part III); the linked PDF is the Commission's report containing the text.

documents.title: Resolution of the United Nations Commission for India and Pakistan of 5 January 1949 (in UNCIP report S/1196)
documents.issuer: United Nations Commission for India and Pakistan
documents.summary: Set out the principles of a free and impartial plebiscite under a UN-nominated Plebiscite Administrator; with the 13 August 1948 resolution it is the core of the UN record on Kashmir. The linked PDF is the Commission's report containing the text.

documents.title: Security Council Resolution 2231 (2015) endorsing the Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action
documents.summary: Endorsed the Iran nuclear deal (JCPOA) and set up the 'snapback' mechanism for restoring UN sanctions; key to Middle East and non-proliferation current affairs.

documents.title: Security Council Resolution 242 (1967) on the situation in the Middle East
documents.summary: Adopted after the 1967 war, it set the 'land for peace' formula: Israeli withdrawal from territories occupied and the right of every state to live in peace within secure boundaries; the basis of later Arab–Israeli peace efforts.

documents.title: United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change
documents.issuer: United Nations (adopted at New York; opened for signature at the Rio Earth Summit)
documents.summary: The parent climate treaty that set the goal of stabilising greenhouse-gas concentrations and the principle of common but differentiated responsibilities; the COP process meets under it.

documents.title: Kyoto Protocol to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change
documents.issuer: Conference of the Parties to the UNFCCC (COP 3)
documents.summary: Set binding emission-reduction targets for developed (Annex I) countries and created market mechanisms such as the Clean Development Mechanism.

documents.title: Montreal Protocol on Substances that Deplete the Ozone Layer
documents.issuer: Parties to the Vienna Convention for the Protection of the Ozone Layer
documents.summary: Phased out CFCs and other ozone-depleting substances and is regarded as the most successful environmental treaty; the 2016 Kigali Amendment extends it to HFCs.

documents.title: Convention on Biological Diversity
documents.issuer: United Nations Conference on Environment and Development (Rio Earth Summit)
documents.summary: Has three objectives: conservation of biodiversity, sustainable use of its components, and fair sharing of benefits from genetic resources.

documents.title: Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (CBD COP decision 15/4)
documents.issuer: Conference of the Parties to the Convention on Biological Diversity (COP 15)
documents.summary: Sets 23 targets for 2030, including the '30x30' target to protect 30% of land and sea, with a 2050 vision of living in harmony with nature.

documents.title: Convention on Wetlands of International Importance especially as Waterfowl Habitat (Ramsar Convention)
documents.issuer: International Conference on the Conservation of Wetlands and Waterfowl, Ramsar, Iran
documents.summary: The oldest modern global environmental treaty, for conservation and wise use of wetlands; Pakistan has 19 Ramsar sites, including the Indus Delta and Haleji Lake. Linked text is the original as registered in the UN Treaty Series.

documents.title: Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction 2015–2030
documents.issuer: Third UN World Conference on Disaster Risk Reduction (endorsed by the UN General Assembly)
documents.summary: Sets seven global targets and four priorities to reduce disaster risk and losses; the reference framework for Pakistan's NDMA and flood-resilience planning.
documents.source: UN Office for Disaster Risk Reduction

documents.title: Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora
documents.summary: Regulates international trade in endangered species through Appendices I–III, relevant to Pakistan's markhor and pangolin protection. Linked text is the original as registered in the UN Treaty Series.

documents.title: United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification in those Countries Experiencing Serious Drought and/or Desertification, Particularly in Africa
documents.issuer: Intergovernmental Negotiating Committee established by the UN General Assembly
documents.summary: The only legally binding treaty linking environment and development to land management, targeting desertification and land degradation neutrality; relevant to Pakistan's arid zones.

documents.title: Declaration of the United Nations Conference on the Human Environment (Stockholm Declaration), in Report A/CONF.48/14/Rev.1
documents.issuer: United Nations Conference on the Human Environment
documents.summary: The first global environmental declaration (26 principles), which led to the creation of UNEP; Principle 21 on state responsibility for transboundary harm is a classic.

documents.title: Rio Declaration on Environment and Development (Report A/CONF.151/26/Rev.1, Vol. I)
documents.issuer: United Nations Conference on Environment and Development
documents.summary: 27 principles including sustainable development, the precautionary approach (Principle 15), polluter pays and common but differentiated responsibilities; the linked report also contains Agenda 21.

documents.title: Climate Change 2023: Synthesis Report — Summary for Policymakers (IPCC Sixth Assessment Report)
documents.summary: The authoritative scientific summary of climate change: human-caused warming of about 1.1°C, rising losses, and the need for deep emission cuts this decade; the go-to source for climate facts in essays.

documents.title: Addis Ababa Action Agenda of the Third International Conference on Financing for Development
documents.issuer: Third International Conference on Financing for Development (endorsed by UN General Assembly resolution 69/313)
documents.summary: The framework for financing the SDGs: domestic resource mobilisation, private finance, development aid, trade and debt sustainability.
documents.source: United Nations (Financing for Sustainable Development Office)

documents.title: Marrakesh Agreement Establishing the World Trade Organization
documents.issuer: Uruguay Round Ministerial Meeting of GATT Contracting Parties, Marrakesh
documents.summary: Concluded the Uruguay Round and created the WTO from 1 January 1995, bringing GATT, GATS, TRIPS and dispute settlement under one roof.

documents.title: Articles of Agreement of the International Monetary Fund
documents.issuer: United Nations Monetary and Financial Conference, Bretton Woods (as amended)
documents.summary: The IMF's founding charter from Bretton Woods setting its purposes, quotas, surveillance and lending; useful background for Pakistan's repeated IMF programmes.

documents.title: United Nations Millennium Declaration (A/RES/55/2)
documents.summary: Adopted at the Millennium Summit, it set the values and targets that became the eight Millennium Development Goals (2000–2015), the predecessor of the SDGs.

documents.title: Beijing Declaration and Platform for Action
documents.summary: The most comprehensive global agenda for gender equality, with 12 critical areas of concern from poverty to women in power; a core text for Gender Studies and essays on women's empowerment.

documents.title: Security Council Resolution 1325 (2000) on Women, Peace and Security
documents.summary: First Security Council resolution linking women to peace and security, calling for women's participation in peace processes and protection from conflict-related sexual violence.

documents.title: Charter of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation
documents.issuer: Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (11th Islamic Summit, Dakar; replacing the 1972 Charter)
documents.summary: Founding instrument of the 57-member OIC, setting its objectives, organs and principles; relevant to Pakistan's foreign policy and the OIC Contact Group on Jammu and Kashmir.

documents.title: Charter of the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation
documents.issuer: Heads of State or Government of the SAARC member states, Dhaka
documents.summary: Created SAARC with decisions by unanimity and bilateral/contentious issues excluded from deliberations, which explains much of its stagnation; standard in questions on South Asian regionalism.

documents.title: Charter of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization
documents.issuer: Council of Heads of State of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization, St. Petersburg
documents.summary: Sets the SCO's goals (mutual trust, combating terrorism, separatism and extremism, economic cooperation) and its bodies; Pakistan became a full member in 2017.

documents.title: Treaty of Izmir (Charter of the Economic Cooperation Organization), as revised 1996
documents.issuer: Governments of Iran, Pakistan and Turkey (1977); revised by the ten ECO member states (Izmir, 14 September 1996)
documents.summary: Legal basis of the Economic Cooperation Organization (successor to the 1964 RCD), setting its aims of regional trade, transport and energy cooperation among ten states including Pakistan.

documents.title: Charter of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations
documents.summary: Gave ASEAN legal personality and codified the 'ASEAN Way' of consensus and non-interference; a frequent model in comparisons with SAARC.

documents.title: The North Atlantic Treaty
documents.summary: Founding treaty of NATO; Article 5 collective defence (invoked only after 9/11) is central to Cold War and Russia–Ukraine questions.

documents.title: Constitutive Act of the African Union
documents.issuer: Assembly of Heads of State and Government of the OAU, Lomé
documents.summary: Replaced the OAU with the African Union; Article 4(h) gives the Union the right to intervene in grave circumstances (genocide, war crimes, crimes against humanity), an early form of R2P.

documents.title: Treaty on European Union (consolidated version)
documents.issuer: Member States of the European Communities (signed at Maastricht; amended by Amsterdam, Nice and Lisbon)
documents.summary: Founding treaty of the EU (Maastricht 1992), now in the Lisbon-amended consolidated form; Article 50 (withdrawal) is the legal route used for Brexit.

documents.title: Tashkent Declaration
documents.issuer: Prime Minister of India and President of Pakistan (mediated by the USSR)
documents.summary: Signed on 10 January 1966 after the 1965 war, committing both sides to withdraw to pre-5 August 1965 positions and settle disputes peacefully.

documents.title: Agreement on Bilateral Relations between the Government of India and the Government of Pakistan (Simla Agreement)
documents.issuer: Prime Minister of India and President of Pakistan
documents.summary: Signed on 2 July 1972 after the 1971 war; converted the ceasefire line in Kashmir into the Line of Control and committed both sides to settle differences peacefully through bilateral negotiations; Pakistan announced it could hold it in abeyance in April 2025.

documents.title: Lahore Declaration
documents.issuer: Prime Ministers of India and Pakistan
documents.summary: Signed on 21 February 1999 during Vajpayee's bus visit to Lahore, the first post-1998 accord, pledging nuclear confidence-building measures and dialogue on all issues including Jammu and Kashmir.

documents.title: Agreement for Bringing Peace to Afghanistan between the Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan which is not recognized by the United States as a state and is known as the Taliban and the United States of America (Doha Agreement)
documents.issuer: United States of America and the Taliban
documents.summary: Signed on 29 February 2020, it set the timeline for US/NATO withdrawal in exchange for Taliban counter-terrorism guarantees and intra-Afghan talks; key to Pakistan–Afghanistan and regional security questions.

documents.title: Constitution of the World Health Organization
documents.summary: Defines health as 'a state of complete physical, mental and social well-being' and sets WHO's functions and governance; a standard reference in public-health questions.

documents.title: International Health Regulations (2005), third edition
documents.summary: Legally binding rules for preventing and responding to the international spread of disease, including declaring a Public Health Emergency of International Concern; amended in 2024 after COVID-19.

documents.title: WHO Pandemic Agreement (World Health Assembly resolution WHA78.1)
documents.summary: Adopted on 20 May 2025 to strengthen pandemic prevention, preparedness and response, including equitable access to vaccines and technology transfer; it opens for signature only after the annex on pathogen access and benefit-sharing is adopted.

documents.title: Convention on Cybercrime (Budapest Convention, ETS No. 185)
documents.summary: First international treaty on crimes committed via the internet, harmonising offences and enabling cross-border cooperation; a reference point for Pakistan's Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act 2016.

documents.title: Global Digital Compact (annex to the Pact for the Future, A/RES/79/1)
documents.issuer: United Nations General Assembly (Summit of the Future)
documents.summary: First global framework for digital cooperation and AI governance, covering closing digital divides, data governance and an independent scientific panel on AI.

documents.title: The Pact for the Future (A/RES/79/1)
documents.issuer: United Nations General Assembly (Summit of the Future)
documents.summary: Adopted in September 2024 with the Global Digital Compact and the Declaration on Future Generations; covers UN Security Council reform, international financial architecture and peace and security.

documents.title: Government of India Act 1858
documents.summary: Transferred the government of India from the East India Company to the Crown after the 1857 War of Independence, creating the office of Secretary of State for India. The starting point for constitutional development under direct British rule.

documents.title: Indian Councils Act 1909 (Morley-Minto Reforms)
documents.summary: Enlarged the legislative councils and, through regulations made under it, introduced separate electorates for Muslims. Key to questions on the growth of Muslim political identity.

documents.title: Government of India Act 1919 (Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms)
documents.summary: Introduced dyarchy in the provinces and a bicameral central legislature. Frequently examined alongside the Khilafat and Non-Cooperation movements and the Simon Commission.

documents.title: Government of India Act 1935
documents.summary: Provided provincial autonomy, a proposed all-India federation and the basis of the 1937 elections; adapted as the interim constitution of Pakistan in 1947. A core topic for constitutional history.

documents.title: Statement by the Cabinet Mission and the Viceroy, 16 May 1946 (Cabinet Mission Plan)
documents.issuer: British Cabinet Mission (statement read in the House of Lords)
documents.summary: Proposed a three-tier Indian union with groupings of provinces and rejected a fully sovereign Pakistan; its acceptance and later breakdown shaped the road to partition. This is the full text as read in the House of Lords.

documents.title: Statement of His Majesty's Government on the Transfer of Power in India, 3 June 1947 (3 June / Mountbatten Plan)
documents.issuer: UK Government (Prime Minister Clement Attlee in the House of Commons)
documents.summary: Announced the procedure for partition, including votes in the Punjab and Bengal assemblies and referendums in NWFP and Sylhet. The plan on which the Indian Independence Act was built.

documents.title: Indian Independence Act 1947
documents.summary: Created the independent dominions of Pakistan and India from 15 August 1947 and gave their constituent assemblies full legislative power. The legal birth certificate of Pakistan.

documents.title: Declaration of Independence
documents.summary: Announced the separation of the thirteen colonies from Britain and stated the natural-rights theory of government. Basic to US history and political-thought questions.

documents.title: Constitution of the United States
documents.summary: The oldest written national constitution in force, establishing federalism, separation of powers and checks and balances. Constantly used as a comparison in constitutional-law and political-science answers.

documents.title: The Bill of Rights (First Ten Amendments to the US Constitution)
documents.issuer: United States Congress (ratified by the states in 1791)
documents.summary: The first ten amendments protecting freedoms of speech, religion and the press and the right to due process. A standard reference point for fundamental-rights comparisons.

documents.title: Monroe Doctrine (President James Monroe's Annual Message to Congress)
documents.summary: Warned European powers against further colonisation of, or intervention in, the Americas. Foundation of US hemispheric foreign policy and of isolationism debates.

documents.title: Emancipation Proclamation
documents.summary: Declared enslaved people in the rebelling Confederate states free and changed the purpose of the Civil War. Leads into the 13th Amendment and civil-rights history.

documents.title: Gettysburg Address
documents.summary: Lincoln's short speech at Gettysburg defining the Civil War as a test of government of the people, by the people, for the people. Often quoted in essays on democracy.

documents.title: President Woodrow Wilson's Fourteen Points
documents.summary: Set out US war aims for a just peace, including self-determination, open diplomacy and a League of Nations. Essential for the Paris Peace Conference and liberal internationalism.

documents.title: The Atlantic Charter
documents.issuer: President Franklin D. Roosevelt and Prime Minister Winston Churchill
documents.summary: Joint Anglo-American statement of post-war aims, including self-determination and no territorial aggrandisement. A forerunner of the UN Charter.

documents.title: Truman Doctrine (President Truman's Address before a Joint Session of Congress)
documents.summary: Pledged US support for free peoples resisting subjugation, starting with aid to Greece and Turkey. The opening statement of containment in the Cold War.

documents.title: Marshall Plan (Economic Cooperation Act of 1948)
documents.summary: Funded the economic recovery of Western Europe after the Second World War. A standard case of aid as an instrument of foreign policy in the Cold War.

documents.title: Civil Rights Act of 1964
documents.summary: Outlawed discrimination on the basis of race, colour, religion, sex or national origin in employment and public accommodations. The legislative peak of the civil rights movement.

documents.title: Magna Carta (1215)
documents.summary: Charter limiting royal power and guaranteeing that no free man be punished except by the lawful judgment of his peers or the law of the land. The symbolic origin of the rule of law; this National Archives resource presents the 1215 charter with related documents.

documents.title: Bill of Rights 1689
documents.summary: Settled the Glorious Revolution: limited the Crown, required parliamentary consent for taxation and a standing army, and protected freedom of speech in Parliament. A basis of parliamentary sovereignty.

documents.title: Union with Scotland Act 1706 (Act of Union 1707)
documents.summary: Joined England and Scotland into the Kingdom of Great Britain with one Parliament from 1 May 1707. Background for questions on the formation of the UK and Scottish devolution.

documents.title: Representation of the People Act 1832 (Great Reform Act)
documents.summary: Abolished many rotten boroughs, gave seats to the new industrial towns and widened the franchise. The start of the gradual democratisation of British politics.

documents.title: Parliament Act 1911
documents.summary: Removed the House of Lords' veto over money bills and replaced it with a delaying power for other bills. Established the supremacy of the elected Commons.

documents.title: Statute of Westminster 1931
documents.summary: Gave the self-governing dominions legislative independence from Westminster. Key to the evolution of the Commonwealth and to dominion status in 1947.

documents.title: Treaty of Westphalia: Peace Treaty between the Holy Roman Emperor and the King of France and their respective Allies (Treaty of Münster)
documents.issuer: Holy Roman Emperor, King of France and their allies
documents.summary: Ended the Thirty Years' War and is traditionally seen as the origin of the modern system of sovereign states. A common starting point in international-relations theory; no official online text exists, so this is the Yale Avalon Project transcription.

documents.title: Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen of 26 August 1789
documents.summary: Revolutionary statement of liberty, equality before the law and popular sovereignty, still part of the French constitution. Central to the French Revolution and the history of human rights.

documents.title: Treaty of Peace between the Allied and Associated Powers and Germany (Treaty of Versailles)
documents.issuer: Allied and Associated Powers and Germany
documents.summary: Ended the First World War with Germany, imposed reparations and the war-guilt clause, and contained the Covenant of the League of Nations. Often discussed as a cause of the Second World War; text via the Yale Avalon Project.

documents.title: Schuman Declaration
documents.summary: Proposed pooling French and German coal and steel production, leading to the European Coal and Steel Community. Regarded as the founding statement of European integration.

documents.title: Treaty establishing the European Economic Community (Treaty of Rome)
documents.issuer: Belgium, France, West Germany, Italy, Luxembourg and the Netherlands
documents.summary: Created the European Economic Community and its common market. The legal foundation of today's European Union.

documents.title: Conference on Security and Co-operation in Europe Final Act (Helsinki Final Act)
documents.issuer: Conference on Security and Co-operation in Europe (35 states)
documents.summary: Cold War détente agreement on borders, cooperation and human rights in Europe, which led to the OSCE. Its human-rights provisions encouraged dissident movements in the Eastern bloc.

documents.title: Treaty on European Union (Maastricht Treaty)
documents.issuer: Member States of the European Communities
documents.summary: Created the European Union, EU citizenship and the path to the single currency. Key to post-Cold War European integration.

documents.title: The Farewell Pilgrimage of the Prophet (PBUH) and his Sermon at Arafat (Sahih Muslim, Book of Hajj, hadith of Jabir)
documents.issuer: Narrated by Jabir ibn Abdullah; compiled by Imam Muslim
documents.summary: Authentic hadith recording the Prophet's sermon at Arafat on the sanctity of life and property, abolition of usury and blood feuds, and the rights of women. Frequently cited as an Islamic charter of human rights.

documents.title: The Treaty of al-Hudaybiyyah (Sahih al-Bukhari, Book of Conditions)
documents.issuer: Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) and the Quraysh of Makkah; narration compiled by Imam al-Bukhari
documents.summary: Authentic hadith narrating the truce between the Muslims and the Quraysh and its terms. Studied as a model of Islamic diplomacy and treaty-making.

documents.title: Cairo Declaration on Human Rights in Islam
documents.issuer: Organisation of the Islamic Conference (19th Islamic Conference of Foreign Ministers)
documents.summary: OIC statement of human rights within the framework of the Shariah, adopted in Cairo on 5 August 1990. Used for comparing Islamic and UDHR-based human-rights frameworks.

documents.title: New Urban Agenda
documents.issuer: Habitat III Conference (Quito); endorsed by UN General Assembly resolution 71/256
documents.summary: Global framework for sustainable, inclusive urbanisation adopted at Habitat III. The key international reference for town-planning answers.

documents.title: Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting
documents.summary: Sets out the objective of financial reporting, the qualitative characteristics of useful information and the definitions of assets, liabilities, income and expenses. The theoretical base of the IFRS standards adopted in Pakistan.

documents.title: Handbook of International Quality Management, Auditing, Review, Other Assurance, and Related Services Pronouncements (2025 edition)
documents.issuer: International Auditing and Assurance Standards Board
documents.summary: Official compilation of the International Standards on Auditing (ISAs) and quality-management standards. The source for auditing questions on audit evidence, reporting and risk assessment.

documents.title: Basel III: International regulatory framework for banks
documents.issuer: Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (Bank for International Settlements)
documents.summary: Post-2008 global standards on bank capital, leverage and liquidity, implemented in Pakistan by the State Bank. Relevant to banking, financial crises and monetary economics.

documents.title: UNESCO Universal Declaration on Cultural Diversity
documents.summary: Recognises cultural diversity as the common heritage of humanity and links it to human rights and development. Useful for anthropology, sociology and globalisation essays.

documents.title: Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence
documents.summary: The first global standard on AI ethics, covering human rights, transparency, fairness and data governance. Relevant to computer-science and current-affairs questions on AI regulation.

documents.title: Windhoek Declaration for the Development of a Free, Independent and Pluralistic Press
documents.issuer: UNESCO seminar on promoting an independent and pluralistic African press (endorsed by the UNESCO General Conference, 1991)
documents.summary: Defined an independent and pluralistic press as essential to democracy; its date, 3 May, became World Press Freedom Day. A standard reference for media-freedom questions.

documents.title: United Nations Standard Minimum Rules for the Treatment of Prisoners (the Nelson Mandela Rules)
documents.summary: Revised UN minimum standards on prison conditions, discipline, health care and the prohibition of torture. The core reference for criminology and prison-reform questions.

documents.title: Fundamental Principles of Official Statistics
documents.issuer: UN Statistical Commission; endorsed by UN General Assembly resolution 68/261
documents.summary: Ten principles on the impartiality, professional independence and confidentiality of official statistics. Relevant to statistics and to the governance of bodies like the Pakistan Bureau of Statistics.

documents.title: Comprehensive Mental Health Action Plan 2013–2030
documents.summary: WHO's global plan for mental-health leadership, community-based services, promotion and prevention, extended to 2030. The main international reference for psychology and public-health questions.

documents.title: International Treaty on Plant Genetic Resources for Food and Agriculture
documents.summary: Treaty on the conservation and sustainable use of crop genetic resources, farmers' rights and benefit-sharing (in force 2004). Relevant to agriculture, botany and food-security questions.

documents.title: Voluntary Guidelines on the Responsible Governance of Tenure of Land, Fisheries and Forests in the Context of National Food Security
documents.summary: International guidance on secure and fair rights to land, fisheries and forests. Useful for land reform, food security and forestry questions.

documents.title: IUCN Red List Categories and Criteria, Version 3.1
documents.issuer: International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN Species Survival Commission)
documents.summary: Defines the extinction-risk categories (Critically Endangered, Endangered, Vulnerable and others) and the criteria used to assign them. The standard reference for zoology, botany and biodiversity questions.
